title: An Isolated Act of Dishonesty Doesn't Have to End Your Career — And Now There's a Published Case to Prove It
excerpt: A published California appellate decision limits when a single act of dishonesty can justify firing a peace officer, and what it means for POST decertification cases.

title: The City Tried to Skip the Bargaining Table on Your Pension. The Court Sent Back the Bill.
excerpt: A California appellate ruling confirms that when a city unilaterally changes pension reciprocity, it still owes employees a seat at the table — and a check to make up the difference.

title: Banked Your Vacation Hours for Retirement? The California Supreme Court Just Redrew the Math.
excerpt: The California Supreme Court limits how much banked leave can count toward your final pension calculation under PEPRA — even if your final compensation period spans two calendar years.

title: Monday-Morning Quarterbacking a Life-or-Death Decision: Why One Appeals Court Finally Said Enough
excerpt: A Texas appellate reversal reinforces the reasonable-officer standard that also governs California's deadly force law, rejecting hindsight-driven second-guessing of split-second decisions.

title: The Supreme Court Just Staked Hawaii's "Vampire Rule" Through the Heart — California Should Take Notice
excerpt: The U.S. Supreme Court strikes down Hawaii's default ban on concealed carry at private property open to the public, closing off a workaround California had been eyeing for its own restrictions.

title: A Bill Meant to Rein In Federal Agents Could Leave California Officers Holding the Bag
excerpt: Senate Bill 747 aims to hold federal agents accountable, but its current language could create a second, murkier standard of qualified immunity for California's own peace officers.

title: Those Minutes Before Roll Call? The Feds Just Said They Count
excerpt: A new federal opinion letter confirms that essential pre- and post-shift tasks like gear checks and equipment prep are compensable work, not free time.

title: A Federal Court Just Narrowed a Wage Claim — Here's Why California First Responders Don't Need to Panic
excerpt: A Third Circuit ruling narrows federal 'gap time' wage claims in that circuit, but Ninth Circuit precedent and California wage law keep the door open for California police and fire employees.

title: Before Your Personnel File Goes Public, Shouldn't Someone Have to Tell You?
excerpt: A New York labor board ruling says agencies must bargain over advance notice before releasing personnel records — persuasive authority for California officers under Penal Code 832.7.

title: Trying to Switch Unions Through the Back Door? PERB Just Nailed That Door Shut
excerpt: Two PERB decisions confirm that severance petitions can only be used to create a brand-new standalone bargaining unit — not to transfer classifications into an existing one.

title: Disciplined AND Retaliated Against? Why Losing One Fight Doesn't Mean You Lose the War
excerpt: An appellate ruling confirms that an arbitrator can order back pay for union retaliation even after a state personnel board has already upheld the same discipline on other grounds.
